html:
The Latin Empire was the state set up in Constantinople by the knights of the Fourth Crusade after they captured the Byzantine capital in 1204. It lasted until 1261.

The crusaders had been diverted to Constantinople by a Byzantine prince's promise of money and by their debts to Venice. When the promises failed, they stormed and looted the city; see Sack of Constantinople. Baldwin of Flanders was crowned emperor in Hagia Sophia. The leaders split the empire: Venice took ports and islands, and Latin lords set up states in Greece. A Catholic patriarch replaced the Orthodox one, which the Greeks bitterly resented.

The empire was weak from the start. Baldwin was captured by the Bulgarians in 1205 and died in prison. Greek successor states rose around it: the Empire of Nicaea under Theodore I Laskaris, Epirus in the west and Trebizond on the Black Sea. By the 1230s the Latin emperors held little beyond the city, and Baldwin II went round Europe begging for money and pawning relics.

In 1261 Nicaea's emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos, who had won Genoa's help in the Treaty of Nymphaeum, sent a small force that found the city poorly guarded and took it; see Constantinople retaken. The restored Byzantine Empire never fully recovered.
sum: The Latin Empire was the state set up in Constantinople by the knights of the Fourth Crusade after they captured the Byzantine capital in 1204. It lasted until 1261.
